why: Quote verified verbatim at headless.md:33-58 (the <Note> line 58 is the whole sentence, nothing reverses it). The cited identifiers are also correct: apps/cli/src/index.ts:78-165 has no '--bare' case, printHelp (:2019-2036) lists no such flag, and `grep -an -- "--bare"` over apps/packages/docs/scripts returns nothing. But the CONSEQUENCE is false, in the exact shape this repo's audit history warns about: the capability bare mode names is already delivered one layer up, under the flag Claude itself documents for it. headless.md:35 defines bare mode as 'reduce startup time by skipping auto-discovery of hooks, skills, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, and CLAUDE.md'. `nessy-general-agent --safe-mode run ...` suppresses a strict SUPERSET of that list: SAFE_MODE_SUPPRESSED_SURFACES (packages/shared/src/config/safe-mode.ts:73-85) is instructions, skills, plugins, hooks, mcp-servers, commands, agents, output-styles, workflows, lsp-servers, memory. The finding's own characterization -- 'an empty-capability-input funnel, not a startup-cost profile' -- is contradicted by the gate's placement: storage-runtime.ts:628-630 returns SAFE_MODE_INPUTS before any read, commented 'Placed before every read so a compromised plugin bundle, skill or .mcp.json is not even opened'. Not opening the files IS the startup-cost reduction bare mode advertises; empty-inputs and skip-discovery are the same mechanism described from two ends. The flag is fully wired end to end (index.ts:129-131 parse, :179 env fallback, :619 exported into the spawned server, :607 prints the suppression list to stderr), and index.ts:612-616 states in-code that 'run is our non-interactive -p mode'. Second refuting axis, product difference: this fork's CLI has no '-p' or '--print' either -- the flag switch at :78-165 shows the non-interactive surface is the 'run' subcommand on the renamed 'nessy-general-agent' binary. Faulting a deliberately renamed CLI for lacking a flag whose host flag it also lacks is a naming observation, not a contract gap; the doc's own clause is forward-looking ('will become the default for -p in a future release'), i.e. Claude roadmap, not present contract. Not one of the nine owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (checked; unrelated). Residual difference is real but far narrower than 'gap': safe mode does not skip OAuth/keychain reads and does not narrow the tool set to Bash/read/edit, and the run path defaults to bypassPermissions -- though '--provider/--api-key/--base-url' plus PROVIDER_ENV_KEYS (index.ts:633+) give the explicit-credential operation bare mode's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY guidance calls for. That residual is a 'partial', not the claimed absence.
correctedState: Bare mode's headline behaviour is implemented, under a different documented flag name. `nessy-general-agent --safe-mode run ...` skips auto-discovery of CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins, hooks, MCP servers and auto memory -- a superset of headless.md:35's bare list -- via a single gate placed before every read (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:628-630 returning SAFE_MODE_INPUTS), which is the same not-reading that produces bare mode's faster start. The literal `--bare` spelling is absent, as is `-p` itself: this fork's non-interactive surface is the `run` subcommand on the renamed `nessy-general-agent` binary, so flag-name parity with `claude -p` is not the contract. Two genuine sub-differences remain and should be tracked as a 'partial' rather than a missing flag: safe mode does not skip OAuth/keychain reads (bare mode does; our equivalent is passing --provider/--api-key/--base-url explicitly), and it does not restrict the tool set to Bash/file-read/file-edit (`run` defaults to bypassPermissions with the full set).
